conviction_note: The company re-guided Q3 on 2026-09-16, two weeks before quarter end: NII at the high end of +4-6% and fees at the high end of +12-14%. The $7.99-8.01B revenue consensus already sits there, so the print itself is mostly told. My own arithmetic puts EPS at about $1.37 against a $1.32 bar even after the ~$160M Amazon reserve build. Against that sit a weak big-bank tape (JPM/BAC revenue misses, WFC NII light and reserve builds), Q3 buybacks paused for capital as the 10-year rose about 50-60bp (AOCI), a name that has fallen on 6 of 7 prints, and downside-paid skew. Small offsetting findings sum to -0.3. p_up is 46 and abs_move_pct is 3.0 (option-implied 3.13% against a historical median of 1.59%), giving -0.24.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $1.32 and revenue ~$7.99-8.01B. Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/USB/earnings-forecasts ($1.32 / $7.99B), TickerLeague https://tickerleague.com/companies/USB/estimates ($1.32, 12 analysts, range $1.24-1.40) and the Zacks preview ($1.32, $8.01B) agree; AAII 2026-10-13 shows $1.33. The company's own guide, measured on Q3 2025 (NII $4,251M, fees $3,078M, expense $4,197M from the Q2 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036104/000003610426000039/a2q26earningsrelease.htm), implies revenue of $7.87-8.02B, and the 2026-09-16 update moved it to the top end. The bar is sourced, so no cap applies.
positioning_check: Short interest is 25.96M shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, ~1.7% of shares outstanding, 2.80 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA https://equibles.com/stocks/usb/short-interest, via the sweep row, read 2026-10-14). That is not a crowded short, so there is no squeeze mechanism. The baseline's 25-delta skew is +3.18 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.74, and the event-implied move is 3.13%, against a median reaction of 1.59% and a maximum of 5.64% over 7 prints. The stock fell on 6 of 7 prints (only Q2 2026 rose, +1.59%) and is -6.6% over 20 days, -14.7% from its 52-week high, and -10.3% from the 2026-07-16 print to 10-12 (AAII). Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) as of 2026-09-21.

findings.finding: At the Barclays conference on 2026-09-16, CFO Stern guided Q3 NII growth to the high end of +4-6% YoY (Q3'25 NII $4,251M, so ~$4.50B), fee growth to the high end of +12-14% and possibly above it on capital-markets timing (Q3'25 $3,078M, so ~$3.51B), and expenses to about +8% (~$4.53B). That puts revenue near $8.0B and PPNR near $3.48B, against Q2'26's $3.28B, which printed $1.35 EPS. Even after the ~$160M Amazon reserve build, the arithmetic gives about $1.37 EPS against the $1.32 consensus. The beat is modest and lies inside guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat $1.35 against $1.27 and raised the FY revenue guide to +7-9%; the stock rose +1.59%, its only up print of 7. Every other print fell 0.04-5.64%, including beats (baseline; Chartmill headline 'Modest Earnings Beat But Stock Slips').
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue consensus ($7.99-8.01B) already reflects the top end of the guide. What may not be is the EPS: $1.32 is below Q2's $1.35 even though guided PPNR is ~$200M higher. If the market had priced the guide-implied EPS, the consensus would sit nearer $1.36-1.38, and the stock would not be down 10% since the last print on an unchanged estimate (AAII: no revisions in the last month). The gap may be explained by tax, preferred dividends or BTIG integration costs (~$30M) that I cannot verify, so the finding is kept small.
findings.independence: Zacks via Yahoo, 2026-09-21, reports the same 'high end' NII/fee update and NIM improving in Q3 and Q4: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/u-bancorp-eyes-strong-q3-153800483.html. It is the same management event, so it does not count as an independent fact.

findings.finding: Buybacks were paused in Q3 for capital needs. Stern called the pause temporary and kept a 70-75% payout target (2026-09-16), after $200M a quarter in Q1-Q2. At June 30, CET1 was 10.8%, or 9.4% including AOCI, with the Category II transition ahead. The 10-year rose from roughly 4.5% at end-June to 5.04% on 09-15 and 5.11% on 09-23, a 16-year high. That implies an AOCI hit to tangible book and to CET1 including AOCI in the Q3 release, plus Amazon-portfolio risk-weighted assets. Resumption timing is the forward line on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved USB print turned on buybacks in the baseline history. Wolfe downgraded USB earlier on its plan to accrete capital and slow buybacks ahead of Category II (undated TipRanks/The Fly item, not used for size).
findings.why_not_priced: The pause is public and the stock is down ~10% since July, so the pause itself is largely priced. What is not yet visible is the size of the Q3 AOCI and CET1 hit and whether management gives a restart date. If that were priced, the stock would not have traded flat to the sector in late September; the week to 09-18 was -4.4% (Fintel), which looks like the market only partly digesting the pause.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript (CET1 10.8% / 9.4% incl. AOCI; buybacks to 'glide up' toward ~10% CET1; Category II transition upcoming): https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/us-bancorp-usb-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/. 10-year at 5.11% on 2026-09-23: https://statisticsoftheworld.com/news/2026-09-23. The AOCI-to-capital step is my inference; USB has not quantified it.

findings.finding: The big-bank prints after USB last spoke (10/13-14) were soft on NII and revenue, with reserve builds. WFC NII was $12.517B against a ~$12.63B consensus, deposit costs rose, and provision of $1.029B was +51% YoY on C&I and auto allowance builds. JPM missed revenue and EPS ($5.57 against $5.93), and its interest-bearing deposit rate rose from 2.11% to 2.18% q/q. BAC missed revenue ($29.96B against $30.58B), with NII reportedly below estimate, and fell ~4% premarket on 10/14. USB has large C&I, auto and card books and the same deposit-pricing exposure after the September hike.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-10-16), printed in a week of regional-bank credit scares (ZION/WAL), fell -1.72%. In Jan 2025 it fell -5.64% the week big banks reported well. Sector tone has dominated USB's prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer prints landed 1-2 sessions before USB, and USB's guide (2026-09-16) predates both the September Fed hike and these prints. If fully priced, USB would already have moved with BAC's -4% today. The baseline spot was struck at 10:00 ET on 10/14, inside the BAC reaction, so part of it may not be in the sealed price. It is still a proxy: USB re-guided NII two weeks before quarter end, which caps the transmission.
findings.independence: JPM 3Q26 supplement (IB deposit rate 2.18% against 2.11%): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026065582/a3q26erfex992supplement.htm. BAC revenue miss and premarket fall: https://247wallst.com/cards/bank-of-america-q3-2026-earnings-bac-01m4x0nj8jz5wveh8jkame6x53. Fortune on the September Fed hike and Dimon's 'sticky inflation' warning: https://fortune.com/2026/10/13/jpmorgan-goldman-sachs-citigroup-wells-fargo-interest-inflation/. These are separate documents from different counterparties.

findings.finding: The Amazon Business card portfolio moved to USB in mid-August (transition set to begin 2026-08-14). Management guided a ~$160M reserve build when it closed, plus $75-85M of quarterly revenue, about two-thirds NII, half of it in Q3. The build adds roughly $0.08/share to Q3 provision, and the guide already includes it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found for USB on portfolio-acquisition reserve builds.
findings.why_not_priced: It is probably priced: it explains why the $1.32 consensus sits below Q2's $1.35. It is filed because a build above $160M, or a day-1 CECL charge on a larger portfolio, would show up as a provision miss. If the market had doubts, EPS estimates would have been cut, and AAII shows no revisions in the last month.
findings.independence: Transition timing and $75M quarterly revenue: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/u-bank-mastercard-amazons-small-124500210.html and https://www.americanbanker.com/news/purchase-of-investment-bank-gave-u-s-bank-a-rapid-boost (2026-07-16).

findings.finding: Management guided merchant processing (Elavon, $485M in Q2, +2.3% YoY) to roughly flat YoY for the next two to three quarters, on European softness and the loss of non-strategic distribution partners. The Payments segment's net income fell to $225M from $235M YoY in Q2. Card issuing and corporate payments are growing (card revenue +5.3%) and offset part of it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: merchant slowdown flagged and the stock still rose +1.59% on fees and capital markets. Payments has not set the reaction on recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is guided and priced; it is filed because a decline rather than flat would be the negative surprise in the fee line. It is a segment item: the rest of fees (BTIG ~$200M/qtr, capital markets, trust, card) is guided to carry total fees to the top of +12-14%, so net of the rest it is close to zero.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K segment detail (merchant +2.3%, Payments net income $225M against $235M): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036104/000003610426000039/a2q26earningsrelease.htm.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp in September 2026 to 3.75-4.00%, and long yields hit multi-year highs, steepening the curve. USB reprices ~$10-11B of fixed assets each quarter at 100-125bp higher yields. Management expects NIM to improve in Q3 and Q4, with a 3% NIM 'at some point in 2027', and the Amazon portfolio's NII is fully in from Q4. The Q4 NII guide and the NIM path are where this could show.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 raised its revenue guide and the stock rose +1.59%; Q1 2026 (-1.58%) and Q4 2025 (-0.04%) gave no large reaction to NII guidance either way.
findings.why_not_priced: USB's last guide predates the hike and the end-September yield peak, and the stock has fallen with the sector on rate fears rather than repricing upward on margin. If the market had priced a better NII trajectory, USB would not be -14.7% from its high while consensus NII is unchanged. The offset is deposit costs rising at peers (finding 3), which this finding is sized net of.
findings.independence: Fortune 2026-10-13 confirms the Fed hike: https://fortune.com/2026/10/13/jpmorgan-goldman-sachs-citigroup-wells-fargo-interest-inflation/. Zacks 2026-09-21 reports NIM expected to improve in Q3 and Q4: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/u-bancorp-eyes-strong-q3-153800483.html.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly negative, which agrees with the +3.18 downside-paid skew and the name's habit of falling on prints. Cutting against them, the stock is already -10% since the last print with no estimate cuts, and the company pre-guided Q3 to the top of its ranges, so I keep p_up near 50 (46) rather than leaning harder.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (a finding inside the guided range): trimmed the guide-implied EPS beat from +0.5 to +0.4; the bar is sourced from two agreeing estimate sources, so no cap.
Lesson 5 (a proxy is filed small): cut the peer read-through from -0.6 to -0.5 and the rate/NIM guidance finding from +0.5 to +0.4.
Lesson 2 (size one-offs as one-offs) and lesson 6 (inside guidance): the guided Amazon reserve build went from -0.2 to -0.1.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): merchant processing went from -0.2 to -0.1, because guided total fees at the top of +12-14% offset it.

Lesson 3 (my own caveat has to reach the number): the capital-return finding went from -0.5 to -0.4, because its own text says the pause is public and largely priced; the AOCI step is inference (lesson 5).
Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction; this name sells prints), weighed against the pessimism-artefact note: kept p_up near 50, 45 to 46, and abs_move_pct unchanged at 3.0.
Lesson 7: looked up short interest (1.7%, 2.8 days to cover, not crowded), so no negative is shrunk for squeeze risk; the sign agrees with the +3.18 skew.
Net: impact_sum went from -0.5 to -0.3 and expected_move_pct from -0.30 to -0.24.
